strategies.name: Unit Test — Isolation
strategies.description: Test a single function or method in complete isolation from its dependencies using mocks, stubs, or fakes.
structural_signals: pure function with no side effects
applies_when: function has clear inputs and outputs
dependencies can be replaced with test doubles
testing internal logic independent of infrastructure
avoid_when: function is a thin wrapper around an external call

strategies.name: Unit Test — Parameterized
strategies.description: Run the same test logic against multiple input/output pairs, covering edge cases efficiently without code duplication.
structural_signals: function with many edge cases on same signature
testing isolated function logic with known inputs
applies_when: same function needs testing with many input variations
boundary values and edge cases are well-defined
test logic is identical across cases
avoid_when: each case requires different setup or assertions
test readability suffers from too many parameters
trade_offs: Failure messages can be less descriptive
May obscure what each case is testing

strategies.name: Unit Test — Table-Driven
strategies.description: Define test cases as a structured table of inputs, expected outputs, and optional descriptions, iterating over each row.
structural_signals: need to document expected behavior as a truth table
testing a parser or transformer with varied inputs
applies_when: Go-style testing or when test data is tabular
cases map naturally to rows in a table
avoid_when: tests need unique setup per case
trade_offs: Very easy to add new cases
Hard to debug when one row of many fails

strategies.name: Unit Test — Exception/Error Path
strategies.description: Verify that functions raise correct exceptions, return proper error codes, or handle invalid inputs gracefully.
applies_when: function has explicit error handling paths
avoid_when: error paths are trivial or auto-generated
exceptions are caught and silently swallowed upstream
trade_offs: Can become verbose for many error types

strategies.name: Unit Test — Async/Concurrent
strategies.description: Test asynchronous functions, coroutines, or concurrent code paths including race conditions and timeout handling.
applies_when: code uses async/await, promises, or threads
avoid_when: async is just a thin wrapper
synchronous equivalent would test the same logic

strategies.name: Integration Test — Database
strategies.description: Test code that interacts with a real database, verifying queries, migrations, transactions, and data integrity.
structural_signals: repository pattern with real data store
applies_when: data access layer needs validation against real DB
complex queries with joins or aggregations
avoid_when: unit tests with mocked repositories suffice
trade_offs: Catches real query bugs that mocks miss

strategies.name: Integration Test — API
strategies.description: Test HTTP endpoints with a running server, verifying request/response cycles, middleware, authentication, and serialization.
applies_when: API contract must be verified end-to-end
avoid_when: endpoint is a pass-through to a service
trade_offs: Can replace many unit tests of handlers

strategies.name: Integration Test — Message Queue
strategies.description: Test producers and consumers against a real or emulated message broker, verifying delivery, ordering, and retry semantics.
applies_when: message format and routing must be verified
consumer retry and dead-letter behavior matters
avoid_when: messages are fire-and-forget with no business logic
broker is abstracted behind a simple interface
trade_offs: Slow and flaky if broker is unreliable

strategies.name: Integration Test — External Service
strategies.description: Test interactions with third-party APIs or external services using sandboxes, recorded fixtures, or staging environments.
applies_when: external API contract changes could break your code
retry and error handling for external calls needs testing
sandbox or staging environment is available
avoid_when: contract tests already cover the interface
cost per API call is prohibitive
trade_offs: Flaky due to network and service availability

strategies.name: E2E Test — Happy Path
strategies.description: Simulate the primary user journey through the application, verifying the most common successful workflow end-to-end.
structural_signals: main workflow from login to completion
applies_when: core user flow must never break
acceptance criteria define a clear path
avoid_when: flow is already covered by integration tests
trade_offs: Highest confidence that the system works

strategies.name: E2E Test — Critical Path
strategies.description: Test the critical business paths that, if broken, would cause revenue loss or user-facing outages.
avoid_when: path is not revenue or compliance critical
lower-level tests already cover the logic
trade_offs: Worth the cost for critical paths

strategies.name: E2E Test — Cross-Browser
strategies.description: Run end-to-end tests across multiple browsers and devices to catch rendering and behavior inconsistencies.
structural_signals: web application with diverse browser support
applies_when: browser-specific bugs have been found before

strategies.name: Contract Test — Consumer-Driven
strategies.description: Consumers define the contract they expect from a provider; the provider verifies it can satisfy all consumer contracts.
structural_signals: multiple consumers of the same provider
applies_when: services are owned by different teams
API changes could break downstream consumers

strategies.name: Contract Test — Provider Verification
strategies.description: Provider service verifies it fulfills the contracts published by its consumers, running against real provider implementation.
applies_when: provider wants to verify it won't break consumers before deploying
CI pipeline includes contract verification step
avoid_when: provider has a single tightly coupled consumer
trade_offs: Depends on consumers publishing accurate contracts

strategies.name: Property-Based Test — Fuzzing
strategies.description: Generate random inputs and verify that universal properties hold across all of them, finding edge cases humans miss.
structural_signals: invariant that must hold for all inputs
applies_when: input space is large and edge cases are hard to enumerate
universal properties can be stated (e.g., encode then decode equals identity)
parser or serializer needs robustness testing
avoid_when: function has complex preconditions hard to generate for
trade_offs: Requires thinking in properties not examples

strategies.name: Property-Based Test — Invariant
strategies.description: Assert that specific invariants (ordering, uniqueness, bounds) hold after any sequence of operations on a stateful system.
structural_signals: sorted collection must stay sorted after mutations
balance properties in trees or queues
state machine with known valid states
avoid_when: state space is too large to explore meaningfully
trade_offs: Harder to write than example-based tests

strategies.name: Mutation Test — First Order
strategies.description: Introduce single-point mutations (flip operators, remove statements, change constants) to verify that existing tests catch them.
structural_signals: measuring test suite quality beyond code coverage
critical code path with high coverage but uncertain quality
applies_when: code coverage is high but confidence is low
want to measure test suite effectiveness
avoid_when: test suite is still being built
code changes too frequently for stable mutation scores

strategies.name: Mutation Test — Higher Order
strategies.description: Combine multiple first-order mutations to find subtle bugs that only manifest when two or more defects interact.
applies_when: first-order mutation testing yields diminishing returns
avoid_when: first-order mutation score is still low

strategies.name: Snapshot Test — Component
strategies.description: Capture the rendered output of a UI component and compare against a stored snapshot, flagging unintended changes.
avoid_when: component output changes frequently by design

strategies.name: Snapshot Test — API Response
strategies.description: Capture API response bodies and compare against stored snapshots to detect unintended schema or data changes.
applies_when: API response format must remain stable
detecting accidental field removal or type change
avoid_when: response contains timestamps or random IDs
response shape changes often by design
contract tests already cover the schema

strategies.name: Load Test — Spike
strategies.description: Simulate a sudden traffic spike to test how the system handles rapid scaling and whether it recovers gracefully.
structural_signals: system exposed to viral traffic patterns
applies_when: system may face sudden traffic bursts
rate limiting behavior must be verified

strategies.name: Load Test — Soak (Endurance)
strategies.description: Run sustained moderate load over an extended period to detect memory leaks, connection pool exhaustion, and gradual degradation.
applies_when: service runs for hours or days without restart
connection or resource pool exhaustion is a concern
avoid_when: time budget for testing is limited
trade_offs: Finds leaks invisible in short tests

strategies.name: Load Test — Stress
strategies.description: Push the system beyond its expected capacity to find breaking points and verify graceful degradation under extreme load.
trade_offs: Can cause cascading failures in shared environments

strategies.name: Load Test — Capacity
strategies.description: Determine the maximum sustainable throughput the system can handle while meeting SLA targets for latency and error rate.
applies_when: SLAs define latency and throughput targets
avoid_when: no defined SLAs or performance targets
system is not yet stable enough for benchmarking
trade_offs: Must be re-run after significant changes

strategies.name: Security Test — SAST
strategies.description: Static analysis of source code to detect security vulnerabilities like SQL injection, XSS, and insecure cryptography without executing the code.
structural_signals: source code with potential injection points
user input flowing to sensitive sinks
static security scanning in CI pipeline

strategies.name: Security Test — DAST
strategies.description: Dynamic analysis of a running application by sending malicious requests to discover vulnerabilities like XSS, CSRF, and injection flaws.
applies_when: application is deployed or can be run locally
avoid_when: API-only service better tested with API security tools

strategies.name: Security Test — Dependency Scan
strategies.description: Scan project dependencies for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and license compliance issues.
applies_when: supply chain attacks are a concern
avoid_when: dependencies are vendored and audited manually

strategies.name: Security Test — Penetration
strategies.description: Simulate real-world attacks against the application to identify exploitable vulnerabilities that automated tools miss.
avoid_when: application is internal only with low risk
budget does not allow professional pen testing

strategies.name: Accessibility Test — WCAG AA
strategies.description: Automated checks against WCAG 2.1 AA criteria including color contrast, ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and semantic HTML.
structural_signals: color contrast and ARIA attribute checking
avoid_when: internal tool with known user capabilities
trade_offs: Must be supplemented with manual testing

strategies.name: Accessibility Test — Screen Reader
strategies.description: Test application usability with screen readers and assistive technologies, verifying reading order, announcements, and focus management.
applies_when: interactive widgets need screen reader support
dynamic content must be announced properly
avoid_when: static content with semantic HTML suffices
automated WCAG checks cover the scope

strategies.name: Visual Regression — Pixel Diff
strategies.description: Capture screenshots of UI components or pages and compare pixel-by-pixel against baselines to detect unintended visual changes.
applies_when: CSS changes may have unintended side effects

strategies.name: Visual Regression — Layout Shift
strategies.description: Detect unexpected layout shifts and cumulative layout shift (CLS) by measuring element positions before and after rendering.
applies_when: Core Web Vitals are a ranking factor
ad or dynamic content shifts page elements
avoid_when: static page with no dynamic loading

strategies.name: API Test — Schema Validation
strategies.description: Validate API requests and responses against OpenAPI/JSON Schema definitions to ensure contract compliance.
applies_when: API has a formal schema definition
multiple consumers rely on the schema
avoid_when: schema changes faster than tests can track

strategies.name: API Test — Idempotency
strategies.description: Verify that repeating the same API request produces the same result and does not create duplicate side effects.
applies_when: API operations must be safely retried
network failures may cause duplicate requests
avoid_when: endpoint is inherently non-idempotent by design

strategies.name: API Test — Rate Limiting
strategies.description: Verify that rate limiting, throttling, and quota enforcement work correctly under various request patterns.
avoid_when: internal API with trusted callers only

strategies.name: Agent Test — Prompt Regression
strategies.description: Run the same prompts against an agent across versions and measure output variance to detect unintended behavioral changes from prompt or model updates.
applies_when: output quality must remain above a threshold
avoid_when: agent is in early exploration phase
outputs are inherently creative with no quality baseline

strategies.name: Agent Test — Tool Call Validation
strategies.description: Verify that an agent selects the correct tools, passes valid parameters, and invokes them in the right order for a given task.
applies_when: agent has access to multiple tools
correct tool selection is critical for task success
tool parameters must be accurately extracted
avoid_when: single tool with no parameter variation
trade_offs: Tool API changes require test updates
Can use recorded traces for replay

strategies.name: Agent Test — Multi-Turn Consistency
strategies.description: Test that an agent maintains coherent state, context, and personality across multiple conversation turns without contradiction or amnesia.
applies_when: context from prior turns affects responses
agent must remember user preferences or stated facts
trade_offs: Complex test setup with conversation scripts

strategies.name: Agent Test — Hallucination Detection
strategies.description: Verify that agent outputs are factually grounded in provided context and do not fabricate information, citations, or capabilities.
applies_when: agent must only state facts from provided context
avoid_when: no source documents to ground against

strategies.name: Agent Test — Determinism
strategies.description: Measure output variance across multiple runs of the same prompt to ensure acceptable consistency for production use.
applies_when: agent is used in automated pipelines
trade_offs: Requires multiple runs per test case

strategies.name: Agent Test — Token Budget
strategies.description: Verify that agent prompts, contexts, and responses stay within token limits to avoid truncation and control costs.
applies_when: context window limits are a concern
avoid_when: token budget is not a constraint
model context window is very large relative to usage

strategies.name: Agent Test — Safety/Guardrail
strategies.description: Test that an agent refuses harmful requests, resists jailbreak attempts, and stays within defined behavioral boundaries.
applies_when: agent is user-facing and could be abused

strategies.name: Agent Test — Chain/Pipeline
strategies.description: Test multi-agent pipelines where output of one agent feeds into another, verifying end-to-end pipeline integrity and error propagation.
structural_signals: output of one agent as input to another
applies_when: error in one stage must not corrupt downstream
trade_offs: Failures hard to localize across agents

strategies.name: Agent Test — Stream Validation
strategies.description: Verify that streamed agent responses are complete, properly chunked, and that partial outputs are valid at every point.
applies_when: agent responses are streamed to clients
avoid_when: responses are delivered in a single batch

strategies.name: Agent Test — Latency Profiling
strategies.description: Measure response time distribution across agent calls, identifying p50/p95/p99 latencies and detecting timeout-prone prompts.
applies_when: user experience depends on response speed
avoid_when: batch processing with no real-time requirement

strategies.name: Agent Test — Context Window Management
strategies.description: Test agent behavior as conversation history approaches context window limits, verifying graceful summarization or truncation.
applies_when: behavior at window limits must be predictable
avoid_when: context window is effectively unlimited for use case
trade_offs: Expensive to test with large contexts

strategies.name: Agent Test — Grounding/Citation Accuracy
strategies.description: Verify that agent-generated citations, references, and source attributions accurately correspond to the content they claim to reference.
applies_when: legal or compliance requirement for traceability
knowledge base retrieval must be verifiable
